articles.decoder: * **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**: A protocol enabling AI agents to connect securely to local files and software tools for a more grounded development process.

articles.title: How Mother Design turned a séance into a new identity for Purple Garden
articles.description: Mother Design began Purple Garden's rebrand with a séance, chakra reading, and automatic drawing workshop, using the resulting forms and feelings to build an identity around spirituality as “A Living Practice.” A whimsical wordmark, crystal-like guidance glyph, warm purple palette, tactile imagery, living typography inspired by cymatic patterns, and expressive motion create an immersive system without relying on familiar psychic-industry clichés. The process moved between physical experimentation, traditional design software, and AI tools, deliberately introducing unpredictability into both the creative process and the finished identity.
articles.one-liner: Mother Design rebranded the psychic platform Purple Garden using unconventional, ritual-inspired techniques and AI to prioritize experimental spontaneity over industry clichés.

summary.what: The studio used séances, chakra readings, and automatic drawing as a starting point for a visual system that includes custom typography, a warm purple palette, and motion inspired by cymatic patterns.
summary.why: This project illustrates a shift toward using AI not just for efficiency, but as a catalyst for creative unpredictability within a structured branding process.

articles.decoder: * **Cymatic patterns**: Visual representations of sound waves manifesting as geometric patterns, used here as the inspiration for the brand's 'living' typography.

articles.title: The New York Times turns 175 with an identity, events and a campaign
articles.description: The New York Times is marking its 175th anniversary with a visual identity, campaign, and program of events that use the publication's history as material rather than simply commemorating its age. Familiar elements from its editorial and typographic heritage are reframed across contemporary applications, connecting decades of journalism with the publication's current cultural role. The system demonstrates how an established institution can celebrate recognizable brand equity while giving historical assets new relevance instead of replacing them.
articles.one-liner: The New York Times is celebrating its 175th anniversary by framing its vast historical archive as a contemporary, active design system.

summary.what: The publication is using a new visual identity, event series, and campaign that reframes its typographic and editorial heritage to maintain brand relevance while celebrating its long history.
summary.why: This shows how legacy institutions can refresh their identity by treating archives as functional design assets rather than static historical markers.

articles.title: This Creative Agency's Website is Giving Me Tumblr 2000s Vibes, and I'm Here for It
articles.description: Denver's Bound Agency has a handmade, scrapbook-style site by Wunder Werkz that evokes 2000s Tumblr, with a handwritten logo, doodled icons, and tarot cards.
articles.one-liner: Bound Agency’s new website abandons corporate templates for a handmade, 2000s-style Tumblr aesthetic, arguing that personality attracts better clients than SEO-optimized landing pages.

summary.what: Bound Agency, based in Denver, worked with the studio Wunder Werkz to replace their traditional agency site with a scrapbook-style interface featuring hand-drawn icons, custom tarot cards, and curated personal playlists.
summary.why: This indicates a growing rejection of 'standardized' web design, where studios are prioritizing authentic brand signaling over lead-generation metrics to filter clients by shared taste.

articles.title: struggle together
articles.description: AI can remove much of the difficulty involved in learning and making things, but some of that struggle builds judgment, understanding, relationships, and the ability to create things with other people that none could have made alone.
articles.one-liner: Over-reliance on AI to eliminate friction in creative work threatens to erase the 'struggle' that builds personal judgment and collaborative social bonds.

summary.what: Developer Ryo Lu argues that the difficulty inherent in learning and creation is not a bug to be patched by LLMs, but a feature that fosters deeper understanding and professional relationships.
summary.why: The industry is approaching an inflection point where the ease of generation may lead to a workforce that lacks the foundational 'taste' and social friction required for original, high-stakes collaborative engineering.

articles.title: Stefan Sagmeister's Artworks Turn Global Data into Good News at La Gaîté Lyrique
articles.description: Stefan Sagmeister's solo show "Finally, Something Good" at La Gaîté Lyrique turns UN and World Bank data into artworks arguing that health, democracy, and equality have improved.
articles.one-liner: Designer Stefan Sagmeister is visualizing long-term global progress by transforming UN and World Bank datasets into physical artworks.

summary.what: Sagmeister's exhibition 'Finally, Something Good' at La Gaîté Lyrique in Paris uses historical trend data to visualize improvements in global health, democracy, and equality, countering the pessimistic trends often seen in media.
summary.why: This approach highlights a trend of using data visualization to provide objective, long-term optimism in public-facing art, contrasting with the often inflammatory and reactive nature of digital information consumption.
